It has been about 20 months, and like so many others have experienced, this freezer died on me. I took a chance with all the bad reviews, though there were not so many when I bought it.

My unit would power on, turn the compressor on, then shut the compressor off after a few seconds. This cycle repeated, with no cooling whatsoever. On the reviews for the white version of this freezer, someone had done a similar repair.

Once I received the part, it took less than 5 minutes to fix. If your remove the old relay, and it rattles when you shake it, you know it is bad. It is located on the side of the compressor, under a plastic cover, towards the front of the machine. Remove the access cover near the cord to see the compressor.

Easy fix. they should have included an extra one with the freezer--it would have saved them a lot of headaches over at RCA/Igloo.

I have had the freezer for a little less than a year and a half. I went into the garage the other afternoon to grab some food for dinner. The freezer was not running and my food was thawing.

I put everything on ice and started looking at the freezer. Both the power light and run light were on but the compressor was not running.

I pulled the compressor start relay and tested it. It was defective.

I called Curtis International's customer service, who manufactures the freezer for Igloo. I gave them all the information about the freezer and asked for a transfer to the parts department or a technician. I was informed that they do not transfer calls, but another department would email me. Three days later, I received an email asking for exactly the same information I gave over the phone.

I provided all the information along with a picture of the broken part. I was informed that because the freezer was beyond the one year warranty, Curtis International would provide no support. They suggested I call a local repair person.

For anyone who has a similar problem, the compressor start relay is part number qp2-4.7g12. You can find it on many part supply websites.
